title: Notebooks
tagline: Notebooks connected to the local database, in JupyterLab, Marimo or your Positron - one folder per persona.
role: Installs Exasol's notebook connector (the package AI Lab is built on), pyexasol, the Langfuse and OpenAI clients, the kit's notebook helpers and a Jupyter kernel named 'Exasol (Starter Kit)' in an environment of their own, and its notebook tools - child rows under it in the marketplace's add-ons table, all three ticked: JupyterLab (yours is used; with none, the kit's is installed because it was ticked), Marimo (installed into the kit's notebook environment) and Positron (yours, only ever configured: the notebooks folder names the kit's Python as its interpreter; the kit never installs Positron).
credentials: The connection lives in the connector's encrypted configuration store (~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebook/connection.scs). Its master password and the JupyterLab and Marimo login tokens are kit credentials in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials, readable by you only. The kernel's spec names only those two file paths, and the helpers read them, so no kernel spec, notebook or output ever holds a secret. The notebooks connect as the kit's admin user, because building tables and UDFs needs it.
installed_by: exakit marketplace notebook (EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=notebook for a script).
platforms: macOS on Apple silicon, Linux x86_64 (including WSL) and Windows x86_64. The connector supports Python 3.11 and 3.12; the kit's managed interpreter is 3.12. Linux on Arm is not offered: one of the connector's dependencies publishes no Linux Arm build.

quickstart.note: About 1 GB: the connector brings PyTorch for its transformer features (the CPU-only build on Linux). Its notebook tools are child rows under it in the add-ons table: JupyterLab, Marimo, Positron - all ticked, each saying what will become of it; untick any you do not want.

On a terminal it asks which tools to open - one multi-select, each row saying its tool's state (running, ready, missing, not installed; Positron found, or where to get it) - and opens each one picked: JupyterLab and Marimo in the background, opened in your browser, logged in, Positron on the folder. Without a terminal it opens JupyterLab. The notebooks are in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks: the kit's in starter-kit-notebooks/, one folder per persona (general, data-scientist, ml-engineer), with a README naming the end-to-end path.
The same notebooks as Marimo notebooks, from notebooks/marimo/<persona>/.
Your Positron, opened on the notebooks folder with the kit's Python as the interpreter.

commands.summary: On a terminal, ask which notebook tools to open (JupyterLab, Marimo, Positron - each row saying its state, Skip opens nothing) and open them; without one, start JupyterLab in the background, connected, and open it. Before anything opens it checks the notebook environment, the database, the connection store, the kernel and the notebooks folder, and fixes or offers what is wrong. marimo does the same for Marimo (installing it when you say yes), positron opens your Positron on the notebooks with the kit's Python; stop stops JupyterLab and Marimo (stop marimo only Marimo); check proves the connection; setup settles a tool without starting it; --port names JupyterLab's port (no menu).

notes: exakit notebook on a terminal asks 'Open which notebook tools?': JupyterLab ('running at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab', 'ready (the kit's <version>)', 'ready (yours: <path>)' or 'missing - reinstall it into the kit's environment'), Marimo ('running at ...', 'ready' or 'not installed - installs it') and Positron ('found - opens on the notebooks folder', or a row that cannot be picked saying where to get it), with Skip to open nothing. The tools you chose at install are ticked (JupyterLab when none). Each one picked opens in turn, one line each with its address, then one line says how to stop them. Without a terminal (a script, an AI agent) nothing is asked: it opens JupyterLab, and a problem it cannot fix there is one line naming the command that does, with a non-zero exit.

The notebook tools are child rows of the notebook in the marketplace's add-ons table, all three ticked: each says before anything installs what will become of it, and then how it settled (a scripted install that draws no table asks one checklist instead). A JupyterLab already on your machine is used as it is; the kit only adds its kernel, 'Exasol (Starter Kit)', which VS Code and other Jupyter front ends offer too. Marimo goes into the kit's notebook environment. Positron is never installed: when it is there, the notebooks folder is set to the kit's Python (.vscode/settings.json, your other settings kept); when it is not, the folder is ready for it (https://positron.posit.co/download.html). For a script: EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_FRONTENDS=jupyterlab,marimo,positron (or none); EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_JUPYTER=skip or EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_MARIMO=skip leaves one out. Untick one now, add it later with exakit notebook setup, marimo or positron.
In Jupyter choose the kernel 'Exasol (Starter Kit)' for a notebook of your own. In Marimo, Positron or a plain script the kit's notebook Python finds the connection by itself.

In a notebook: import exakit.nb as nb; conn = nb.connect() opens the database, nb.sql(conn, '...') runs a query into a DataFrame and remembers it, and nb.show_sql() prints the last statement. nb.load_own_file(path, table, descriptor) loads your own CSV, Parquet or JSON file the same way the reference datasets are described. (exakit_nb, the older name, still imports.)

Model-call tracing is opt-in: with LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_HOST set before exakit notebook, nb.trace(...) records the calls in your own Langfuse project. Without them it says tracing is off and does nothing else.

Exasol's AI Lab notebooks that use only the database run here. Those that upload to BucketFS, install the Transformers or Text AI extensions or deploy a container through BucketFS do not: a local Exasol Personal database has no BucketFS upload service. Use exakit udf-file and exakit udf-use instead.
A notebook you edited is never overwritten: an update copies only notebooks you do not have yet.
An AI Lab or a JupyterLab of your own on the same machine is left alone.

data-scientist/01_explore runs on any dataset with a descriptor: set DATASET in its first code cell to pharma_trials, banking_complaints, the path of your own descriptor.yaml, or a CSV/Parquet/JSON file with <name>.descriptor.yaml beside it - one assignment and no SQL changes. Every query is built from the descriptor's roles and printed before its result; a small scikit-learn model trains on this computer; its text step sends a few rows to your own model endpoint only when EXAKIT_NB_MODEL is set (endpoint and key in OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY), traced to your Langfuse when the LANGFUSE_* variables are set, and it asks before sending rows of a live (virtual schema) source.

ml-engineer/01_train trains a text classifier inside the database with a Python UDF and logs the run with exasol-mlflow from the notebook (with exasol_mlflow.start_run(conn, ...) as run: run.execute(sql)): parameters, metrics, the training SQL, the model file and the session, statement and deployment it came from. The run goes to MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI when set before exakit notebook, else to a local MLflow store in the mlflow folder beside the notebook. ml-engineer/03_score_external_model brings a model trained anywhere in with exakit model put and scores it with the udf-devkit's scoring UDF template.

The kit's notebooks, one folder per persona, in the order to open them (the requirements document's catalogue): data-scientist/00_quickstart and 01_explore (Data Scientist), ml-engineer/00_quickstart, 01_train and 03_score_external_model (ML Engineer); 00_shared holds the cells both quickstarts use (connection check, schemas, one loader per way data arrives: a sample dataset, your own file, a connected source). Each quickstart checks what its persona depends on first. What goes where is notebook/catalog.json in the kit: adding a notebook is one entry there and its file, no code.

Versions: the connector is pinned in the kit's versions.json (components.notebook), and so are the JupyterLab and Marimo the kit installs (components.notebook.frontends; JupyterLab comes in through the connector's [jupyter] extra). exakit update notebook moves them to new pins and always refreshes the kit's own helpers. EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_VERSION, EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_JUPYTERLAB_VERSION and EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_MARIMO_VERSION override a pin.
exakit uninstall keeps your notebooks (~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks, the mlflow stores beside them included); EXAKIT_UNINSTALL_NOTEBOOKS=remove removes them too.

troubleshooting.symptom: exakit notebook says the database is not running, or the connection to it was lost
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit start - On a terminal exakit notebook offers to start it itself, then rewrites the notebooks' connection and checks it; if the notebooks still cannot connect nothing is opened - see exakit status and exakit logs.

troubleshooting.symptom: JupyterLab was deleted, or is not installed, so the notebooks have nothing to open in
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit notebook setup - Its row in the menu says 'missing'; picking it offers to reinstall the kit's JupyterLab at its pinned version. Without a terminal, setup installs it without asking.

troubleshooting.symptom: Marimo was deleted from the kit's notebook environment
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit notebook marimo - It offers to install it again (yes is the default, and the answer without a terminal).

troubleshooting.symptom: The notebook environment is missing or broken (its Python is gone, or the connector does not import)
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit update notebook - On a terminal exakit notebook offers the same repair: the notebook environment installed again (about 1 GB).

troubleshooting.symptom: Positron shows as 'not on this machine'
troubleshooting.remedy: Get it at https://positron.posit.co/download.html. The notebooks folder keeps its Positron settings; once Positron is back, exakit notebook positron opens it.

troubleshooting.symptom: Port 8888 (or Marimo's 2718) is in use by another program
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit notebook - Without --port the next free port (up to 20 above) is used, said, and remembered. A port named with --port is refused when it is taken: pick another, e.g. exakit notebook --port 8890.
exakit notebook - It is made again with the kit's notebooks. A single kit notebook you deleted from a folder that is still there is not copied back.

troubleshooting.symptom: The notebooks' connection store or its master password was deleted
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit notebook - A new store is written from the kit's connection (the old one cannot be read without its master password; one that would not open is kept as connection.scs.unreadable).

troubleshooting.symptom: The kernel 'Exasol (Starter Kit)' is gone from Jupyter
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit notebook setup - Every exakit notebook registers it again.
exakit notebook --no-browser - It prints the address; the login token is in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials (notebook_jupyter_token, notebook_marimo_token) - never paste it anywhere else.

troubleshooting.symptom: No connection to the kit's database was found
exakit notebook says the add-on is not installed
JupyterLab did not answer in time
01_explore says the descriptor does not match the database
